chapter_seo_title: Dao Twisted World Ch. 301: The Scariest Monster is the Bureaucracy
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang, now an official of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, visits a county magistrate to find the missing villagers. The road to the truth is paved with willow twigs, bribery, and a terrible shock: the Office itself is the suspect.
og_title: The Bureaucracy Is the Real Horror in Dao Twisted World Ch. 301
og_description: Forget monsters. Li Huowang faces a county magistrate who forgot an entire village vanished.
twitter_title: Ch. 301: The Bureaucratic Sludge of the Dao-Twisted World
twitter_description: Li Huowang just learned: the office he works for took the victims.

lore_anchors.definition: The chief official of a county in imperial China, serving as judge, tax collector, and administrator.
A private secretary hired by a local official, skilled in law, paperwork, and political maneuvering.
The head of the county’s police force; responsible for arrests, patrols, and local investigations.
An imperial agency in the Dao-Twisted World that polices supernatural activities and rogue cultivators.
A chilled, jelly-like noodle dish, often served as a summer refreshment in traditional Chinese cuisine.
A wheel-less passenger carriage carried by bearers; a symbol of status and official rank in pre-modern China.
A token or badge worn at the waist signifying one’s official identity; used as identification and authority.
A fictional high-end restaurant or banquet venue referenced in the novel as a place for apology feasts.
